column4: A satellite photograph looking straight down from orbit (orthographic map view, no perspective, no horizon) at scattered fair-weather clouds over a pitch black night sea: many separate clouds of all sizes, small puffs and big lumpy clusters, frayed edges, the thick middles bright white, the thin edges dim grey, plenty of pure black sea between them, evenly spread over the whole square, the same scale everywhere, no land, no text, seamless on all four sides.

A satellite photograph looking straight down from orbit (orthographic map view, no perspective, no horizon) at a broken storm overcast over a pitch black night sea: big torn masses and long ragged bands of cloud stretched one way by the wind, cracks and holes of pure black sea through it, the thick parts bright white, the thin parts dim grey, evenly spread over the whole square, the same scale everywhere, no land, no text, seamless on all four sides.
